Valuation follows evidence.

CoatChex asked $200K for 10% on Shark Tank, a $2M valuation, with no venue customers yet. Mark Cuban offered $200K for 33%, about a $600K valuation. The founder countered at 20% and Mark walked.

With no customers, the buyer sets the price. If you want a higher number, bring revenue, not projections.

You don't have to sell the company to build value.

Cousins Maine Lobster took $55K for 15% from Barbara Corcoran on Shark Tank. Instead of selling, they franchised: franchisees fund the trucks, with an initial investment of roughly $187K to $493K per the franchise disclosure document. The brand now runs 80+ food trucks in 30+ states, plus restaurants.

The right structure can let you grow on other people's capital.

Growth funded with debt has a deadline.

Tom+Chee took $600K for 30% from two Sharks, a $2M valuation. After the show the deal changed, the chain pushed into franchising, and it couldn't repay a loan. In 2017 Gold Star Chili bought the assets from the lender, terms not disclosed.

Before you expand, know your runway and the order in which everyone gets paid.
